text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.28% today to close at $145.64, holding near its recent highs despite oil prices falling. The mild gain came even as crude dropped on hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East — Brent has retreated from its recent spike above $109 after Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities. The stock's real strength lies in its two-week surge of 12.6%, which reflects the substantial oil price rally that preceded today's pullback; with global crude at $126.55 per barrel (well above typical levels), the company benefits from higher revenues regardless of day-to-day swings.

The broader context here is Middle East risk premium — geopolitical tensions around Iran, Houthis, and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have driven oil prices sharply higher over the past weeks, and that tailwind still supports energy stocks even when traders rotate out on occasional optimism about de-escalation.
